categories.main_business_segments: Fulin Precision Co., Ltd. primarily operates in three main business segments: automotive engine precision parts manufacturing, new energy vehicle intelligent electronic control components, and lithium-ion battery cathode materials production. The automotive parts include precision hydraulic components and electromagnetic valves for engines and transmissions. The new energy vehicle segment focuses on intelligent thermal management systems, electronic pumps, and electric drive reducers. The lithium battery cathode materials segment specializes in lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode materials for electric vehicles and energy storage.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company employs advanced manufacturing technologies such as precision hydraulic processing, laser automatic welding, high-precision machining, and automated assembly. For lithium iron phosphate cathode materials, it uses a solid-phase synthesis combined with ferrous oxalate technology, which avoids carbon thermal reduction, resulting in uniform carbon coating and superior product performance. The production process emphasizes high compaction density, high capacity, and long cycle life. The company also integrates lean production and fine management to improve efficiency and reduce costs.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Fulin serves over 60 domestic and international automotive OEMs, including major Chinese brands like BYD, SAIC, Geely, Great Wall, and new energy vehicle leaders such as NIO, Li Auto, and XPeng. It also supplies joint ventures like Volkswagen, General Motors, and Toyota, as well as overseas customers including Renault, PSA, and Audi. The lithium battery cathode materials are supplied to leading battery manufacturers such as CATL and Hive Energy. The company targets mid-to-high-end automotive OEMs and energy storage markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in China with manufacturing bases in Mianyang, Sichuan Province, and subsidiaries in Jiangxi, Hunan, and Sichuan. It has a wholly-owned subsidiary in Europe (France) to serve overseas markets. Domestic sales dominate, accounting for over 96% of revenue, with growing exports to Europe, North America, and other regions. The company is expanding production capacity in Jiangxi and Jiangsu provinces to support growth.
categories.supply_chain_position: Fulin operates mainly in the midstream segment of the automotive and lithium battery supply chains. It manufactures key precision components for automotive engines and transmissions, as well as critical electronic control parts for new energy vehicles. In the lithium battery industry, it produces cathode materials, a core upstream input for battery cell manufacturers. The company also engages in some upstream raw material supply collaborations to secure lithium carbonate and precursor materials.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus is on accelerating the transition to new energy and intelligent automotive components, expanding intelligent thermal management and electric drive systems, and upgrading lithium battery cathode materials technology. R&D priorities include developing high-density, high-capacity LFP and manganese-doped LFP materials, improving low-temperature performance, and reducing costs. It invests in automation, lean manufacturing, and collaborates closely with OEMs and battery makers for synchronized product development. Emerging areas include robotic electric joints and active suspension components.
categories.revenue_model: Fulin generates revenue primarily through direct sales of automotive precision parts, new energy vehicle electronic components, and lithium battery cathode materials. Sales are mostly made via direct contracts with OEMs and battery manufacturers, with some exports through trade companies. The company follows a make-to-order production model based on customer contracts and orders, with pricing linked to raw material costs, especially for lithium battery materials.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In automotive engine parts, Fulin competes with global suppliers such as INA (Germany), BorgWarner (USA), Eaton (USA), NTN (Japan), and Delphi (USA). In new energy vehicle electronic components, it leverages early technological advantages and partnerships with leading domestic OEMs to strengthen its market position. In lithium battery cathode materials, it is a leading domestic producer of LFP materials with proprietary ferrous oxalate technology, competing in a market with rapid capacity expansion and price volatility. The company positions itself as a cost-competitive, quality-focused supplier with strong R&D and supply chain integration.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2023, Fulin reported total revenue of approximately RMB 5.76 billion, a 21.58% decrease from 2022, mainly due to a downturn in lithium battery cathode material prices and demand. Net profit attributable to shareholders was a loss of RMB 542.7 million, a significant decline from the previous year’s profit. Automotive parts revenue grew by 19.63%, while lithium battery materials revenue declined by 42.44%. The company’s total assets reached RMB 9.1 billion, with a net asset decrease of 16.06%. Despite short-term challenges, the company is investing in capacity expansion and new product development to capture growth in new energy sectors.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Fulin emphasizes its technological innovation, cost control, and supply chain advantages to deliver high-quality, precision automotive components and advanced lithium battery cathode materials. Its proprietary ferrous oxalate LFP technology offers superior performance with high compaction density, long cycle life, and safety, favored by high-end EV manufacturers. The company’s close collaboration with leading OEMs and battery makers enables rapid product iteration and customization. Its lean manufacturing and quality management systems ensure competitive pricing and reliable delivery, positioning it as a trusted partner in the evolving automotive and energy storage markets.
